events.title: The birth of Michelangelo
events.shortBlurb: The sculptor and painter who would carve the Pietà and paint the Sistine Chapel was born in Tuscany…
body: Michelangelo Buonarroti was born on 6 March 1475 at Caprese, a small town in the upper Arno valley where his father was serving as magistrate; the family soon returned to Florence. At thirteen he was apprenticed to the painter Ghirlandaio, and by 1489 he was studying sculpture in the Medici gardens under Bertoldo, a pupil of Donatello, enjoying the favor of Lorenzo the Magnificent.

Called to Rome in 1496, he carved for St Peter's the Pietà of 1499, and for Florence the colossal David. Julius II summoned him back to Rome in 1505; for that pope he painted, almost unaided and against his will, the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel between 1508 and 1512, and for Paul III the Last Judgment on its altar wall, completed in 1541.

In 1546, after the death of Sangallo, Paul III made him chief architect of the new St Peter's; for seventeen years he directed the work and raised the drum of the great dome, which he did not live to see completed. He died at Rome on 18 February 1564, in his eighty-ninth year, and was buried, as he had wished, among his own people in Santa Croce at Florence.
